claims.text: A 60-second apnea-modality window from recording c02, starting at 2000-01-05T05:40:00+00:00 and ending at 2000-01-05T05:41:00+00:00 (window index 340), was flagged as an anomaly by the detector.

The detector classified the window as an anomaly with a reconstruction error of 3.628, exceeding the anomaly threshold of 3.521 by a margin of 0.108 (normalized margin 0.031); the detector semantics note this is reconstruction threshold evidence, not probability or calibrated confidence.

The model is a BiLSTM temporal-attention autoencoder (model version apnea-05-c02_seed2026, fold apnea-05-c02) trained on the apnea dataset with test patient c02; no signal-level or attention-level evidence was available for this window.

In the five minutes preceding the current event, the patient had one prior anomaly at 2000-01-05T05:39:00+00:00 (reconstruction error 3.550) and four normal windows with reconstruction errors between 3.418 and 3.472, indicating a recent rise in reconstruction error leading to the current anomaly.

The aggregate trend from 2000-01-05T04:40:00+00:00 to 2000-01-05T05:35:00+00:00 shows an increasing endpoint direction, with mean reconstruction error rising from 2.140 to 3.464 and a maximum anomaly rate of 0.6 in any bucket, supporting a progressive elevation in reconstruction error.

Across the 340 windows analyzed before the current event, 20 anomalies were recorded (5.9% anomaly rate), with the latest prior anomaly at 2000-01-05T05:39:00+00:00 and a maximum reconstruction error of 129.262, indicating recurrent anomaly activity in this patient.
No clinical context was supplied for this patient; the clinical summary is marked as synthetic_prototype with zero diagnoses and zero visits.

The current anomaly at 05:40 is consistent with a rising reconstruction error trend observed over the past hour and follows a prior anomaly one minute earlier, but no signal-level or attention-level explanation is available, and clinical context is absent.
